items.title: Section: Five Words for Being Alive, and Why Pleasure Keeps the Body Upright

items.zh: 問：依何根處說如是言：眾生存活、住、持、安隱？答：依命根說。有諸氣息，故名眾生。思慮相應，故名存活。等餘而住，故名為住。增上而轉，故說名持。無有病惱，故名安隱。問：依何根處說如是言：平正受，受所攝？答：依喜、樂根說，望所餘受自相、共相、依止相所顯故。
items.en: Question: on what basis did the Blessed One speak of beings living, existing, abiding, sustained, and at ease? Answer: resting on the life faculty. Having breath is called living. Being joined with thought is called existing. Remaining in accordance with prior karma is called abiding. Empowering continuity is called being sustained. Being free of illness is called being at ease. Question: on what basis did the Blessed One speak of an even, upright feeling subsumed under feeling in general? Answer: resting on the faculties of joy and pleasure, revealed in contrast to the remaining feelings' own characteristic, shared nature, and supporting basis.

items.title: Section: A Monk Who Would Not Waver Even If the Buddha Himself Asked Him to Disrobe

items.zh: 如平正等，如是不平正等、非平正非不平正等，如應當知。問：世尊依何根處說如是言：於如來所淨信深固，根生建立，一切世間若諸沙門、若婆羅門、若天魔梵，無有如法能引脫者？答：依信根說。此顯其信，於聞思修勝解堅固義。又此堅固隨所信解方便顯示，謂智、生、主、淨最勝之者，尚不能動，何況凡流。
items.en: As with the even, upright feeling, so too should the uneven, and the neither upright nor uneven, feelings be understood. Question: on what basis did the Blessed One speak of a pure faith in the Tathāgata so deep and firm that no ascetic, brahmin, or heavenly lord of desire or form could lead one away from it through any legitimate means? Answer: resting on the faith faculty. This reveals faith's own firm resolve, cultivated through learning, reflection, and meditation. This firmness is further revealed through whoever is considered most excellent in wisdom, birth, dominion, or purity — since not even such a one could shake it, how much less an ordinary person.

items.zh: 又堅固義復有差別。謂其信深固，由世間善決定勝解為出世勝解根本故，又由出世清淨勝解所建立故。當知最初是標句，後二是釋句。

items.title: Section: Five Faces of Diligence — From Armoured Resolve to Never Being Satisfied

items.zh: 問：世尊依何根處說如是言：住有勢、有勤、有勇健、堅猛、於諸善法中常不捨善軛？答：依精進根說。此精進根，略顯其相差別有五。謂被甲精進、方便精進、不下精進、無動精進、無喜足精進。問：世尊依何根處說如是言：念、等念、隨念、別念、不忘念、心明記、無失、無忘、無失法？答：依念根說。
items.en: Question: on what basis did the Blessed One speak of abiding with strength, effort, courage, and firm resolve, never abandoning the yoke of wholesome practice? Answer: resting on the diligence faculty. This diligence faculty's own characteristic is, in brief, revealed to have five distinctions: armoured diligence, diligence in method, undaunted diligence, unwavering diligence, and diligence without complacent satisfaction. Question: on what basis did the Blessed One speak of memory, even memory, repeated memory, distinct memory, unforgetting memory, clear mental retention, and freedom from loss, forgetting, or error? Answer: resting on the mindfulness faculty.

items.title: Section: Closing the Scriptural Explanations — Mind's Nine Stages of Settling, and Wisdom's Fourfold Investigation

items.zh: 此差別義，如攝異門分應知。問：世尊依何根處說如是言：令心住、等住、安住與近住、調、寂靜、寂止、一趣、等持性？答：依定根說。此差別義，如聲聞地應知。問：世尊依何根處說如是言：簡擇法、極簡擇、遍尋求、遍伺察？答：依慧根說。此差別義，亦如聲聞地應知。所餘善根，信等攝故，其差別義無復可得。問：於幾根處立身念住？答：七。問：於幾根處立受念住？答：五。問：於幾根處立心念住？答：一。問：於幾根處立法念住？答：最後八及命根。
items.en: This distinction should be understood as explained in the Compendium of Synonyms. Question: on what basis did the Blessed One speak of settling, equally settling, abiding, and closely abiding the mind, taming, calming, stilling, one-pointedness, and balanced sustaining? Answer: resting on the concentration faculty, its distinction explained as in the Hearer's Stage. Question: on what basis did the Blessed One speak of investigating phenomena, most thoroughly investigating, comprehensively seeking, and comprehensively scrutinising? Answer: resting on the wisdom faculty, likewise explained as in the Hearer's Stage. The remaining wholesome faculties, being subsumed under faith and the rest, admit no further distinction. Question: on how many faculties is mindfulness of the body established? Answer: seven. Question: of feeling? Answer: five. Question: of mind? Answer: one. Question: of phenomena? Answer: the final eight, together with the life faculty.

items.title: Section: Mapping the Faculties onto the Four Noble Truths

items.zh: 問：幾根最勝苦諦依處？答：九。問：幾根最勝集諦依處？答：五。問：幾根滅諦依處？答：一切。問：幾根道諦依處？答：最後八。
items.en: Question: how many faculties serve as the most excellent basis for the truth of suffering? Answer: nine. Question: for the truth of origin? Answer: five. Question: for the truth of cessation? Answer: all of them. Question: for the truth of the path? Answer: the final eight.

items.title: Section: How Many Faculties Does It Take to Think, Speak, or Act Well?

items.zh: 問：依幾根處善思所思？答：九。問：依幾根處善說所說？答：十。問：依幾根處善作所作？答：十六。如是惡思所思、惡說所說、惡作所作，如應當知。問：幾根最勝惑業依處？答：九。問：依幾根處起煩惱業？答：五。問：依幾根處斷煩惱業？答：最後八。
items.en: Question: on how many faculties does wholesome thinking depend? Answer: nine. Question: wholesome speaking? Answer: ten. Question: wholesome acting? Answer: sixteen. As with these, so too should unwholesome thinking, speaking, and acting be understood. Question: how many faculties serve as the most excellent basis for affliction and karma? Answer: nine. Question: on how many faculties does affliction and karma's arising depend? Answer: five. Question: on how many does severing affliction and karma depend? Answer: the final eight.

items.title: Section: Five Conditions for a Truly Auspicious Life, Beginning with Genuine Patience

items.zh: 問：由幾根故，領納一切世出世間所有吉祥？答：除二。問：由幾根故，領納一切吉祥敗壞？答：十一。問：幾根能引所有吉祥？答：最後八。復次，如世尊言：諸受欲者，略有五種作吉祥法。謂忍辱、柔和、觀人而捨、行賢善行，及不放逸。云何忍辱？謂由三種行相應知。
items.en: Question: on how many faculties does receiving all mundane and transcendent auspiciousness depend? Answer: excepting two. Question: on how many does receiving the collapse of all auspiciousness depend? Answer: eleven. Question: how many faculties draw forth all auspiciousness? Answer: the final eight. Next, as the Blessed One said: those who still enjoy sensory pleasure can, in brief, secure auspiciousness through five conditions — patience, gentleness, discerning restraint towards others, virtuous conduct, and freedom from negligence. What is patience? It should be understood through three aspects.

items.title: Section: Ten Kinds of Patience, and Why Being Gentle Is Not the Same as Being Patient

items.zh: 一、不忿怒，二、不報怨，三、不懷惡。若別分別，乃有十種。一、已受怨害忍，二、現前怨害忍，三、慮恐怨害忍，四、饒益怨憎忍，五、損害親友忍，六、一切怨害忍，七、一切因怨害忍，八、受教怨害忍，九、擇力怨害忍，十、自性怨害忍。如是一切，總說名為耐違害忍。云何柔和？謂性賢善，由身語意將護於他，令無惱害。若他所有無罪喜樂，未生令生，生已隨護；有罪憂苦，若未生者遮令不生，若已生者方便令脫。此中忍辱，耐他違害；柔和，於他不作違損。
items.en: First, not becoming enraged; second, not seeking revenge; third, not harbouring ill will. Distinguished further, there are ten: patience towards already-suffered harm, towards present harm, towards anticipated harm, towards an enemy's benefit, towards harm done to loved ones, comprehensive patience towards all harm, causal patience towards all harm, patience through having been taught, patience through discerning insight, and innate patience. All of these together are called patience enduring harm and opposition. What is gentleness? A genuinely good-natured disposition, protecting others through body, speech, and mind so they suffer no harm. Here, patience endures harm from others; gentleness refrains from inflicting harm on others.

blocks.text: Explanations of scriptural words through the faculties, and a short teaching on what makes a life "auspicious", beginning with patience.
Master Cháng Bǎi: having breath makes one a being; with a breath of air and able to go on living, one is a being.

A monk whose faith would not waver even if the Buddha himself asked him to disrobe. (Untranslated, 0617b07: faith is deep and firm because worldly conviction becomes the root of supramundane conviction, and is established by it.)
Master Cháng Bǎi: strength is armoured diligence; courage, without timidity before vast practice, is undaunted diligence; firmness, unmoved by outer things, is unwavering diligence.
Master Cháng Bǎi: mindfulness held long on one object is concentration; mindfulness is the method.
Master Cháng Bǎi: the physical faculties, mind, and life are the basis of suffering; feelings experience it, and from them love, hate, and karma arise.
Master Cháng Bǎi: evil thinking needs only the mind; evil speech, mind and tongue; mind is part of every act.
Master Cháng Bǎi: give what is most needed, at the right time.
Patience: not raging, not retaliating, not harbouring ill will. "Patience endures harm from others; gentleness does not harm others." Master Cháng Bǎi: patience is passive, gentleness active.
Patience and gentleness are two different virtues. One receives harm without returning it; the other never starts it.

quiz.q: The English has "Having breath is called living. Being joined with thought is called existing." What is the problem?
options: no problem: 眾生 is living and 存活 existing, one-to-one, and the lecture agrees
the sūtra terms are five; the English drops 眾生, using living and existing, shifting the match
氣息 should be "fragrance"
思慮 should be "worry"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: having breath makes one a being; with a breath of air and able to go on living, one is a being. The Chinese defines 眾生 by breath. The English explains "living" by breath and "existing" by thought, so the defined term 眾生 disappears and the five terms no longer line up one to one.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain 受所攝?
options: whatever acts together with feeling, body, mind, or other factors, is subsumed under it
only feeling itself; other mental phenomena are unrelated, and so the phrase cannot extend to body or mind
it means lovely objects
it means what the Buddha experiences
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: what is subsumed under feeling is whatever acts together with feeling, whether body, mind, or other mental factors. The English "subsumed under feeling in general" reads it as a species under a genus, which differs from this reading of what accompanies feeling.

quiz.q: How do the five kinds of diligence match the sūtra's phrases?
options: strength unwavering, effort armoured, courage uncomplacent, firmness method, yoke undaunted
all five match strength
strength armoured, effort method, courage undaunted, firmness unwavering, not leaving the yoke uncomplacent
the five are unrelated to the phrases
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: strength is armoured diligence; courage, without timidity before vast wholesome practice, is undaunted diligence; firmness, unmoved by outer things, is unwavering diligence; never leaving the yoke of wholesome practice is diligence without complacency. The English "diligence in method" matches 有勤.

quiz.q: On how many faculties is each mindfulness established, and why those for phenomena?
options: body five, feeling seven, mind two, phenomena eight; the life faculty belongs under the body, on which it depends, and so it is not counted among phenomena at all
all four on the mind
body one, feeling one, mind one, phenomena nineteen
body seven, feeling five, mind one, phenomena nine; the five with life belong to the phenomena-field, the three under faith and the rest
quiz.why: The treatise gives seven, five, one, and the final eight with life. Master Cháng Bǎi: faith and the rest with the life faculty are in the field of phenomena, and the three uncontaminated faculties fall under faith and the rest. This counts to twenty-two with nothing left over.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi match the terms of mindfulness to the abodes of mind?
options: 念 is taming, 等念 calming, and so on, the abodes being unrelated to mindfulness
all four match the last abode
念 is settling, 等念 equal settling, 隨念 abiding, 別念 close abiding; mindfulness held long on one object is concentration
all four belong to wisdom
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: 念 equals inner settling, 等念 equal settling, 隨念 abiding, and 別念 close abiding; mindfulness long held on a single object is called concentration, mindfulness being the method. The English "memory" in §53 and "settling" in §54 hide this link between the two lists.

quiz.q: How many faculties are the chief bases of the truths of suffering, origin, and path, and which?
options: suffering five: the feelings; origin nine: the physical, mind, and life; path eight
suffering nine: seven physical, mind, life; origin five: the feelings; path eight: five wholesome with the three
suffering eight; origin eight; path six
all three twenty-two
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the seven physical faculties, the mind, and life are the basis of suffering's results; these feelings experience the results, and from them love, hate, and karma arise, making them the basis of origin; the path is the five wholesome faculties with the three uncontaminated ones.

quiz.q: On how many faculties does evil thinking rest, per the lecture, and how do the three karmas relate to mind?
options: evil thinking on nine, speech ten, action sixteen, identical to the good, without further distinction
evil thinking rests on mind alone, evil speech on mind and tongue; no karma is apart from mind
all three rest on the tongue
they rest on no faculty
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: evil thinking needs only the mind; evil speech needs mind and tongue; since none of the three karmas is apart from the mind, it must always be added. The English "unwholesome thinking" is general where the Chinese 思所思 pairs the act and its object.

quiz.q: The English has "discerning restraint towards others" for 觀人而捨. Against §§59–60, what should it mean?
options: observing faults and leaving such people, §59 being about this, so "restraint" fits
it is cultivating equanimity
observing the person, then giving: §60 lists five kinds of giving; "restraint" turns giving into holding back
it is renunciation
quiz.why: §60 explains 捨 as five kinds of giving, and the English there has "Giving." Master Cháng Bǎi: give what is most needed and suitable at the right time; with thought joined to non-greed, body and speech act in giving. So 觀人而捨 is observing people and then giving. "Restraint" in §57 does not connect to this.

quiz.q: What are patience's three aspects, and what is patience towards an enemy's benefit?
options: not killing, stealing, or misconduct; actively benefiting one's enemy, the highest patience
no greed, hatred, delusion; reconciling
not raging, not retaliating, not harbouring ill will; bearing it when someone benefits one's enemy
patience of body, speech, mind; leaving enemies
quiz.why: The three aspects are not raging, not retaliating, and not harbouring ill will. Master Cháng Bǎi: when someone benefits a person one dislikes or resents, one can still be patient; this is the fourth of the ten. The English "patience towards an enemy's benefit" is compact but fits this.

quiz.q: How do patience and gentleness differ, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: patience is passive, bearing harm; gentleness is active, not harming others
patience is active, benefiting first; gentleness is passive, not resisting, and higher
they are exactly the same
patience is of body, gentleness of speech
quiz.why: The treatise distinguishes them directly: patience endures harm from others; gentleness does not harm others. Master Cháng Bǎi: patience is passive, gentleness active. The English here is accurate.
